title: Version affinity and graceful-degrade routing prototype for pinned rollouts
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: We need deterministic, observable routing behavior when customers combine model-version pinning (per-route or per-api-key), gradual rollouts (canary/A-B), and policy-driven region/tier selection. Current behavior is inconsistent in edge cases: e.g., a pinned user travelling between regions may abruptly lose affinity to a canary; fallback rules can bypass pinning during capacity events; and rollout metrics are polluted by routing-level fallbacks. This ticket prototypes a concise arbitration model and a pragmatic implementation strategy that preserves pin intent, enables controlled canaries, and makes graceful degradation explicit.
proposal: High-level arbitration lattice: 1) Honor explicit version pinning first (api_key.route.pin_version). 2) Within pin scope, apply sticky affinity for canary variants if the pin maps to a rollout cohort — i.e., pin+cohort -> resolve to pinned variant if rollout config ties pin to cohort. 3) If no explicit pin, evaluate routing policy stack: (region constraints -> tier constraints -> cohort assignment for rollouts -> capacity-aware variant selection). 4) If capacity constraints or latency SLO violations occur, attempt ordered fallback to model variants declared in the route (primary -> performance-quantized -> smaller-family), but never break an explicit pin unless a hard failure mode (region unreachable) and admin override present. 5) All fallback decisions must emit structured events to the console and incrementable metrics for analysis.
implementation_plan: Phase A: Library/Resolver changes (2 weeks): - Add `RoutingContext` with resolved intent fields (explicit_pin, preferred_region, preferred_tier, cohort_id, affinity_key). - Implement deterministic cohort assignment that can be seeded for canary cohorts so experiments are reproducible across regions. - Implement a variant fallback chain resolver that returns both primary selection and a ranked fallback list. Phase B: Runtime integration (2 weeks): - Integrate resolver into request path with a feature flag `rt.routing.v1.experimental_affinity` - Add telemetry hooks: route.events.fallback, route.events.pinned-hit, route.events.pin-broken. Phase C: Rollout tests and chaos (1 week): - Simulate region outage and capacity storms; assert pinned users keep pin if route defines multi-region fallback; assert console shows fallback events. Phase D: Docs + Console UX (1 week): - Add routing visualization in rollout page showing cohort distribution, pin hits, and fallback counts.
testing_plan: Unit tests for cohort assignment determinism, variant chain ranking, and pin precedence. Integration tests: - Synthetic traffic with pinned API keys moving across regions to assert consistent variant selection. - Canary rollout A/B with sticky session semantics: measure cohort leakage rates <1%. - Capacity-triggered fallback: create resource pressure (emulated GPU saturation) and assert fallback order respected and metrics emitted. E2E: Canary experiment dashboard shows canary conversion vs fallback rate.
rollout_strategy: Gate behind feature flag for internal customers. Start with a single non-critical model family and one region pair (us-east-1, us-west-2). Open the experiment to an initial 5% of traffic (cohort-based) for 48h; monitor pin preservation, latency tail, and fallback events. If fallback events exceed 0.5% or pinned user errors increase, pause rollout and revert feature flag.
metrics_and_observability: Primary metrics: pinned_hit_rate (per-route), fallback_rate (per-variant/pair), cohort_leakage_rate, latency_p50/p95 for pinned vs unpinned. Logs: structured events with fields [request_id, api_key_hash, resolved_version, fallback_chain, region, tier, reason]. Dashboards: add per-route timeline and per-cohort breakdown. Alerts: fallback_rate > 0.5% for 30m -> page oncall; pinned_error_rate > 0.1% -> paging.
open_questions: Should admin override (force-fallback) be a route-level flag or an org-level emergency control?
How to reconcile pinning semantics when a pinned version is intentionally retired (deprecation window)?
Do we need crypto-stable cohort seeds to guarantee cross-region cohort sticky assignment for long-lived sessions?

2026-03-09 - Risk review: fallback events can leak experiment signals; decided to tag all fallback requests with experiment metadata to exclude from rollout metrics unless explicitly configured (Aisha)
